data.title: Tej Johar: SK Hynix U.S. Share Premium Could Narrow
data.description: According to CNBC, Tej Johar, a portfolio manager at Trium Capital, is betting that SK Hynix’s U.S.-listed shares will lose part of their premium to equivalent securities in Seoul and Frankfurt. The premium widened from 13% to about 48% after the company listed on Nasdaq via American depositary receipts in July, as U.S. investors sought exposure to AI companies, Johar said. On Nov. 13, Seoul- and Frankfurt-listed securities closed at about $90, compared with $132 for the U.S. shares. Johar said the typical American depositary receipt premium over the past 25 years was about zero and described the potential trade as an approximately $8 billion alpha opportunity.

data.title: Euro-Area Pay Growth Edged Up Marginally in Third Quarter
data.description: A key measure of euro-area pay growth accelerated only slightly in the third quarter, reassuring the European Central Bank that inflation triggered by rising energy prices is not spreading, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Bending Spoons May Issue Convertible Bonds as Supplementary Funding
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, a person familiar with Bending Spoons said the company is considering issuing convertible bonds as a supplement to its existing funding channels amid high interest rates. Such bonds generally carry lower coupons than conventional bonds of similar ratings, but give bondholders the option to convert them into shares, diluting existing shareholders.

Since listing in July, Bending Spoons has raised funds through debt and equity markets, mainly to acquire more technology companies and operate its expanding portfolio. Its acquisitions include AOL, Eventbrite, Airtable and Vimeo. The company is betting that major restructuring can revive growth at these established brands. Its latest acquisition, collaboration software company Miro, closed in late October at an enterprise valuation of about $1.36 billion, 90% below Miro’s valuation in a 2021 private funding round.

People familiar with the company said past acquisitions typically cost one to seven times the target’s revenue. Bending Spoons is now targeting companies with annual revenue of at least $500 million and deal values in the multibillion-dollar range. It is open to acquisitions across technology, with health technology a particular area of interest. Acquisitions are funded mainly with debt, supplemented by free cash flow and equity. In the first six months of 2026, the company generated about $250 million in free cash flow, compared with $2.3 billion in total acquisition spending.

Bending Spoons aims to keep net leverage at two to three times. At the end of June, net debt was $4.09 billion and leverage was about 2.4 times. The company is due to report third-quarter results this Friday. Moody’s and S&P have assigned it non-investment-grade credit ratings. It secured about $1.7 billion in loans in September, partly to finance the Miro deal, and raised $1.8 billion in its first high-yield bond sale in October. A person familiar with the matter put the blended effective rate on its debt at about 9%.

The company’s funding costs could fall modestly as it builds a public-company track record or if overall interest rates decline. An investment-grade rating could lower borrowing costs further, but would require reduced leverage or other trade-offs; the company has no current plan to pursue that, a source said. Bending Spoons views convertible bonds as supplementary, not a core funding source, because they cannot raise very large sums and the company wants to limit dilution.

Last month, Bending Spoons privately placed $330 million in shares with Berkshire Hathaway, which had invested $600 million in its IPO. Equity issuance helps keep leverage within its target ceiling. After acquisitions, the company lays off employees and assigns 50 to 60 of its own staff to management roles. It has also raised prices at several acquired companies, but has no current plan to raise prices at Airtable, acquired in September.

data.title: Hong Kong Proposes SFC Licensing for Four Types of Virtual Asset Services
data.description: Hong Kong’s government has gazetted the Draft 2026 Virtual Asset Service Legislation (Amendment) Bill. According to Odaily, the proposal would bring virtual asset trading, advisory, management and custody services under licensing or registration by the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC); providers would need to meet fit-and-proper criteria. Banks regulated by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority and licensed stored-value facility operators would also need to register with the SFC to provide any virtual asset services in Hong Kong. The bill is scheduled for its first reading in the Legislative Council on December 2.

data.title: Saudi Arabia Begins Replenishing Crude at Joint Storage Facility in Japan
data.description: According to Jin10, Saudi Arabia has begun replenishing crude oil at its joint storage facility in Japan, the Saudi Press Agency reported.

data.title: Japan Plans to Buy 8 Million Barrels of Saudi Crude to Replenish Oil Reserves
data.description: According to Jin10, the Saudi Press Agency reported that Japan plans to buy 8 million barrels of crude oil from Saudi Arabia to replenish its national oil reserves.

data.title: Joerg Wuttke: Putin's First Trilateral Meeting Was a Major Win
data.description: According to CNBC, Russian President Vladimir Putin joined U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping for their first-ever trilateral meeting on the sidelines of the APEC summit Thursday. Joerg Wuttke of DGA-Albright Stonebridge Group said Putin emerged with stronger standing and described the meeting as a major win for the Russian leader. Putin also held bilateral meetings with at least seven world leaders over the two days, while the war in Ukraine continued with no signs of ending. The three leaders issued a joint declaration of peace, but no concrete agreements on Ukraine were announced. Andrius Tursa, a Teneo adviser, said Putin would likely seek to make the trilateral format permanent.

data.title: AI | Minerva Uses Chinese Open-Weight Models for Specific Use Cases
data.description:
Minerva mixes and matches AI models for specific use cases, co-founder Daniel Saedi said in an interview, according to Bloomberg. He also discussed data sovereignty and the risk of “obliterated models.”

This week, the Trump administration was reportedly considering requiring US companies to disclose publicly whether they use Chinese AI models. Last year, a Chinese company released a cheaper model that appeared nearly as capable as cutting-edge US models, in what became known as the “DeepSeek moment.”

data.title: AI | US Chip Curbs Stir Fresh Volatility Around Nvidia
data.description:
The US imposed new restrictions on China’s access to high-end AI chips after a spying controversy involving Nvidia, setting off fresh volatility in the AI trade during a choppy week for equities, Bloomberg reported.

The curbs threatened a fragile trade truce as President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump met at the APEC leaders’ summit in Shenzhen. Investors also weighed questions about how a leadership shift at Nvidia and global AI policy could affect semiconductor supply chains.

data.title: Lagarde Urges Europe to Address Threats Before They Emerge
data.description: European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde said Europe should prevent threats from materializing rather than wait for crises to unfold, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Norwegian Petroleum Directorate: Norway’s Preliminary October Crude Oil Output Was 1.842 Million Barrels per Day
data.description: According to Jin10, the Norwegian Petroleum Directorate put Norway’s preliminary crude oil production in October at 1.842 million barrels per day.

data.title: Pulsar Enables USDT Deposits on TRON for Everyday Payments
data.description:
Pulsar Money added support for USDT deposits on TRON (TRC-20), allowing users to fund their accounts for everyday payments. Users can spend their balances on online purchases, subscriptions and other expenses through Pulsar’s virtual card, according to BeInCrypto; Pulsar charges no fees for supported stablecoin deposits, though network and third-party fees may apply.

TRON processed $2.21 trillion in stablecoin settlement volume in Q3 2026, averaging $24 billion daily. Pulsar founder and CEO Alex said the integration gives users another way to use their stablecoins in everyday life, while TRON DAO spokesperson Sam Elfarra said it brings TRON’s payment infrastructure closer to everyday use. Features and availability may vary by region and service provider.

data.title: Polish Monetary Policy Council Member Joanna Tyrowicz Says Rates Should Rise Sharply
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, Polish media quoted Monetary Policy Council member Joanna Tyrowicz as saying that interest rates should rise sharply and that the council should clearly communicate a hawkish stance, including that rate increases are not a one-off measure and that the central bank is firmly committed to raising borrowing costs as needed.

Tyrowicz said that a year ago in the summer, when inflation was lower and its trend was improving, she considered interest rates of around 5% insufficient to bring inflation back to its target range. Rates are now lower, she said, while the inflation outlook is concerning.

Poland’s Monetary Policy Council kept its benchmark interest rate unchanged at 3.75% earlier this month.

data.title: Barclays: Hawkish Fed Could Pressure Stocks; AI Slowdown and Sustained Rate Hikes Are Hard to Reconcile
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, Barclays warned on November 20 that global stocks could remain under pressure through year-end if the Federal Reserve sends further hawkish signals or inflation data exceed market expectations. The bank said concern that the Fed may no longer support stock prices poses a bigger challenge than recent volatility in AI-related stocks.

Barclays strategist Emmanuel Cau and his team said strong economic growth and persistently high inflation had prompted a sharp repricing of rate expectations, tightening financial conditions, strengthening the dollar, reducing excess market liquidity and weighing on equity valuations. The bank compared the current environment with December 2018, when stocks fell about 20% before rebounding strongly in early 2019 after the Fed turned dovish.

Markets have fully priced in a Fed rate hike in December, and recent comments by Fed Governor Christopher Waller prompted speculation about a 50-basis-point increase. Barclays economists disagreed, saying a hike of that size would send a panic signal and imply that the Fed had made a mistake by pausing rate increases in October. Markets expect about three rate hikes over the coming year, but Barclays said that outlook conflicts with recent stock-market performance. If the selloff reflects concern that the AI investment cycle is fading, slower AI investment would ultimately weigh on growth, ease overheating pressures and reduce the need for further monetary tightening. Barclays said a marked slowdown in AI investment and a persistently hawkish Fed stance are difficult to sustain together over the long term.

Barclays said financial markets increasingly show late-cycle characteristics, while market performance has diverged somewhat from economic fundamentals. U.S. retail sales and Germany’s ZEW economic sentiment index both exceeded expectations, and corporate earnings continued to grow. Nvidia’s latest results, the bank said, supported the view that the AI capital-spending cycle remains solid. Barclays reiterated that enthusiasm for AI may have peaked, but the investment race is far from over; a late-cycle economy does not mean the expansion is about to end, and recent risk aversion and selling may have gone too far. It said the Fed’s December rate decision and subsequent CPI data will be key to risk appetite, and stocks could remain under pressure through year-end if inflation exceeds expectations or the Fed turns more hawkish.

data.title: South Africa’s Richards Bay Terminal Loads Record Chrome Cargo on Largest Carrier to Visit
data.description: According to Bloomberg, South Africa’s Richards Bay Bulk Terminal loaded a record chrome cargo aboard the largest bulk carrier to call at the facility. The loading was a bright spot in logistics performance as Durban, the country’s biggest port, continues to underperform.

data.title: China Buyers Cancel Palm Oil Cargoes as Storage Space Runs Short
data.description: According to Bloomberg, Chinese buyers have canceled several palm oil cargoes as the country’s inventories hover near a five-year high and storage space runs short. The cancellations add pressure to a market already dealing with excess Malaysian supply.

data.title: XMR1 Falls 99.8% From About $500 to $0.90 After Selloff
data.description: According to ChainCatcher citing Ember Monitoring, an XMR1 deployment wallet transferred 5.2 million tokens to an address. Some of the tokens were subsequently sold, and XMR1’s price fell about 99.8%, from approximately $500 to $0.90.

data.title: Polygon Releases Heimdall v0.14.0 as Purley Hard Fork Activates on Mainnet and Amoy Testnet
data.description:
Polygon has released Heimdall v0.14.0 for mainnet and the Amoy testnet, where the Purley hard fork was activated simultaneously. According to Foresight News, the public release matches the features of the previously distributed v0.14.0-priv version, and its source code has also been made public.

The Purley updates require validator vote extensions to be signed and certified in every block that contains them, and cross-chain bridge events to be confirmed before execution. Staking updates are accepted only at a validator’s next nonce. Expired checkpoint buffers are retained until replaced by newly approved checkpoints, while canceled governance proposals without a target address are no longer charged fees.
